headline.text: Free Gemini drops from three models to one

body.text: Google says via its support page that from Oct. 9, free users lose Flash and Pro. They now pick among three models in a menu. After the change, every free request will use Flash-Lite.

headline.text: Paying $4.99 a month won't keep Pro

body.text: Google says AI Plus subscribers will be limited to Flash-Lite and Flash, with Pro gone. Their date may differ from Oct. 9. Google says it will email them when the change takes effect.

headline.text: Keeping Pro means moving up a plan

body.text: Pro will require AI Pro or AI Ultra. Yahoo calculates that a Plus subscriber who wants to keep it pays roughly $15 more a month, or $180 a year, at current prices.

headline.text: What free users give up

body.text: Google's support page calls Pro its most advanced model, for complex math and coding. It describes Flash-Lite as built for speed and everyday tasks like summarization and brainstorming.

headline.text: Google's second plan overhaul this year

body.text: PCMag says it is the second overhaul of Google's AI plans this year. 9to5Google notes a May usage-limit change came first. PCMag suggests rising costs may play a part. Google has given no reason.

headline.text: Google adds effort levels, and a catch
What is still unclear

body.text: Google hasn't said exactly when Plus users lose Pro. Sources also split on Deep Think: 9to5Google says AI Pro gets it, while Engadget says AI Ultra subscribers do.

caption.text:
Google says that from Oct. 9, Gemini app users without a paid Google AI plan will be limited to the Flash-Lite model and lose access to Flash and Pro. The change appears on Google's support page, as reported by 9to5Google, PCMag and Engadget.

Google AI Plus subscribers ($4.99 a month in the US) will keep Flash-Lite and Flash but lose Pro, on a date Google says it will email them. Pro will require AI Pro or AI Ultra. Yahoo calculates that a Plus subscriber keeping Pro would pay roughly $15 more a month. Google has given no reason for the change. PCMag suggests rising storage and component costs may be a factor, and notes it is Google's second plan overhaul this year. Sources also disagree on whether AI Pro or only AI Ultra gets the Deep Think option.

Would you pay $19.99 a month to keep Pro?

Follow Helios Group to keep track of what Google changes in Gemini next.

Source: 9to5Google, Oct. 3, 2026; PCMag, Oct. 5, 2026; Engadget, Oct. 6, 2026; Yahoo Creators, Oct. 6, 2026.

edit_notes: Cover leads with Google (well_known true) and the Oct. 9 loss of Flash and Pro, kept as Google's claim via support page.
Skipped Q1 as a quote slide (single-source); paraphrased the email point in slide 3 body.
Split stat uses N1 and N2; $15 and $180 attributed to Yahoo's calculation, not computed by us.
Deep Think disagreement between 9to5Google and Engadget shown openly on the final slide, not picked.
Cost explanation attributed to PCMag as a suggestion; noted Google gave no reason. May change used as one background clause (B1).
Left out 4x/5x usage multiple (sources disagree), Gemini 4 Argon, student offer, 1 billion users and survey data to keep the story focused.
Caption names Yahoo's $15 figure; adds no facts beyond slides and brief. Used Q2 whole on the quote slide (two sources).
